question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered read-only configuration layers as a public core Gateway contract, or keep managed composition in launcher, include, or host-specific tooling?
rationale: This introduces a new repeatable CLI surface and a distinct runtime mode that changes reload, mutation, persistence, and ownership semantics; source correctness alone cannot establish the intended long-term product contract.

options.title: Resolve the RFC first
options.body: Pause merge until the managed-configuration RFC establishes the supported core contract, then require the path-scoped ownership repair.

options.title: Sponsor core layers now
options.body: Approve this bounded startup-only direction and ask the contributor to repair owner scoping and refresh integration proof on current main.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Decline the new core flag and retain composition in host launchers or existing include-based configuration workflows.

recommendation.title: Resolve the RFC first
recommendation.body: Pause merge until the managed-configuration RFC establishes the supported core contract, then require the path-scoped ownership repair.
